I found and generated two method comparison syntheses relevant to comparing the modular pipeline, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning approaches across your papers:

1. Synthesis titled "Comparison of Modular Pipeline and Imitation Learning Performance in Autonomous Driving" (id: af66ce35-cb72-53fb-b45e-d33f7e7da2b8)
   - Covers performance differences between modular pipeline and imitation learning, noting less than 10% difference and bimodal performance in modular pipeline based on perception stack success.
   - Highlights challenges in pure imitation learning despite large datasets and improvements from imitation dropout.

2. Synthesis titled "Comparison of Autonomous Driving Methods in CARLA Simulator and ChauffeurNet Studies" (id: c852cecd-1b7c-5934-b073-6940f848b813)
   - Covers comparison of the three approaches (modular pipeline, imitation learning, reinforcement learning) using CARLA simulator.
   - Notes that modular pipeline and imitation learning differ by less than 10% in performance.
   - Points out limitations of pure imitation learning in driving tasks despite high-capacity models and large datasets.

Would you like me to generate a review draft from these syntheses or any further details?
